items.title: Acosta: "Did I break through after the win? Keep your fingers crossed for me!"

items.title: Bastianini: "Acosta's victory brought a more relaxed mood to the pit"
items.author: Andrea Scalera
items.excerpt: "He took advantage of the opportunity, but I'm not comfortable with that tire. I'm glad we'll have the usual one at Motegi. I'm not looking for anything extreme. I always work within that window, but it's a very narrow one."

items.title: Home hero Ai Ogura strong at Motegi, “but not on the MotoGP bike - yet”
items.excerpt: Ai Ogura doubts home knowledge will help at Motegi, but believes hot conditions could provide an advantage in the MotoGP flyaways.

items.title: Di Giannantonio on brakes at Ducati: "We've always had a few minor issues"
items.author: Gianluigi Mazza
items.excerpt: "It's something we always to be careful about. Is Motegi a Ducati track? In today's MotoGP, those kinds of things don't matter anymore. And we'll also have to assess the grip of the new asphalt."

items.title: The Pedro Acosta trait "great riders do" that stunned his KTM crew chief
items.excerpt: Pedro Acosta’s KTM crew chief Paul Trevathan says it is a “scary question” to predict how much further the MotoGP winner can improve.

items.title: Quartararo: “Yamaha’s home race won’t be as satisfying as it will be for KTM”
items.author: Daniela Piazza
items.excerpt: “We’re in a completely different situation than they are. My goal will be to try to make it into Q2 on Friday.”

items.title: Rins, available as a test rider: “A race in 2027? I’ll always be available.”
items.author: Daniela Piazza
items.excerpt: “I would've liked to try out the 850 and the new tires. If they offered me a race next year, I’d consider it.”

items.title: Nicolo Bulega’s emotional first words after winning WorldSBK title
items.excerpt: Nicolo Bulega struggled for words after winning the 2026 WorldSBK title at Cremona.

items.title: Morbidelli: “Cremona? I went to see how you win a World Championship.”
items.author: Riccardo Guglielmetti
items.excerpt: “As of now, all the circuits belong to Ducati or Aprilia. Austria was a special case, but maybe we’ll see a KTM in the mix here, too.”

items.title: Senna Agius: Shame not to share MotoGP grid with Jack Miller
items.excerpt: Senna Agius says he is “incredibly proud” to carry Australia’s MotoGP hopes as Jack Miller prepares to leave the championship.

items.title: Martín: "Help from Acosta? If so, dinner's paid for—and at an expensive restaurant!"
items.author: Marco Caregnato
items.excerpt: "Just kidding—I think Pedro has his own goals, which are to win more races. The 2024 battle with Pecco and this one with Marc aren't any different; I was the underdog back then, too, and I came out on top."

items.title: Iker Lecuona explains Italian WorldSBK qualifying scare that almost cost him pole
items.excerpt: Iker Lecuona says he “did everything the opposite” of what he was told by his crew chief in Italian WorldSBK Superpole.

items.title: Acosta: "It was harder for me to win a race than a World Championship"
items.author: Matteo Aglio
items.excerpt: "Fighting for the title? We're not far behind in terms of points, but we are in terms of speed. My goal is to finish third in the championship—I can't afford to make any mistakes."

items.title: Toprak Razgatlioglu reveals when he thought to “stop racing”
items.excerpt: Toprak Razgatlioglu says his difficult MotoGP rookie season reminds him of 2018, when he even considered stopping racing.

items.title: Ogura: "Help Martín and Bezzecchi? If I have to overtake them, I'll do it."
items.author: Marco Caregnato
items.excerpt: The Japanese rider explains: "That's the situation right now. I think I'm in good shape. It's great to have regained my speed in Austria, and expectations are high here."

items.title: How Alvaro Bautista is trying to generate “more options” for 2027 race seat
items.excerpt: WorldSBK champion Alvaro Bautista says his performance at the end of 2026 will be key to his chances of finding a good race seat for 2027.

items.title: Bezzecchi: "Marc and Jorge are locked in a head-to-head battle; the world championship is anything but easy"
items.author: Marco Caregnato
items.excerpt: "The new asphalt here will be a leap into the unknown for everyone. Right now, I'm focused on regaining the speed I had before my injury, and in the meantime, I hope not to lose points but rather to gain some."

items.title: Nicolo Bulega vows to maintain WorldSBK “approach” despite “big” MotoGP test crash
items.excerpt: Nicolo Bulega says he will not change his “approach” to the Italian WorldSBK weekend despite his title chance and a recent test crash.

items.title: Vinales: “I thought I’d never come back; I didn’t think they’d call me back.”
items.author: Daniela Piazza
items.excerpt: “There’s no room for me here anymore, but I’m not done yet: when I get an opportunity, I’ll take it. My shoulder isn’t fully healed yet, but it should be good enough to ride a MotoGP bike. The 850? It’s a Moto2 bike with a great engine.”

items.title: Marquez: "From here on, we have to attack every time—every point counts."
items.author: Matteo Aglio
items.excerpt: "Why didn't I celebrate my podium finish in the Sprint in Austria? I'm conserving my energy—it's my job." And on Quiles' match point: "He's a killer; he's building his future."

items.title: Bagnaia: "Motegi 2025? 'I had fun riding "my way," just like Frank Sinatra'"
items.author: Riccardo Guglielmetti
items.excerpt: "I was giving it 100%. But it'll be tough—we've been trying for about two seasons now. Bulega? SBK is different from MotoGP; the pace is faster here."

items.title: Bagnaia: "My last win was at Motegi... positive thought as I head into the GP"
items.author: GPOne
items.excerpt: Fond memories of Ducati as the team arrives in Japan. Pecco’s latest victory and Marc Marquez’s 2025 title were both secured here. Different stories, same track.

items.title: Martín: "We're heading into the Asian leg of the season in good form; let's stay focused."
items.author: GPOne
items.excerpt: Jorge on the eve of Motegi: "We're working really well as a team, and I want to thank Aprilia." Bezzecchi: "We were fast here last year."

items.title: Foti: “Bulega? At first, he didn’t trust anyone—I just told him to smile.”
items.author: Riccardo Guglielmetti
items.excerpt: “That day he replied, ‘I’ll do it when I have a reason to.’ When he did his first test on the Superbike, we understood everything—he was already a second off the record.”

items.title: Domenicali: "Ducati will remain in Superbike, but on one condition"
items.author: Matteo Aglio
items.excerpt: "Balancing performance shouldn't prevent the best bike from winning. Bulega's story isn't over yet—this title is just a step along the way."

items.title: Biaggi and Bulega, two rebirths in Superbike: "He managed to find himself again; he can do well in MotoGP"
items.author: GPOne
items.excerpt: Max restarted with Suzuki after a year away from racing, before winning two titles with Aprilia. Bulega rebuilt his career with Ducati and will take on the premier class in 2027.

items.title: Lecuona: "I expect Bulega to be fast right away in MotoGP; he has a lot of experience with Pirelli tyres."
items.author: Gianluigi Mazza
items.excerpt: "It was a perfect weekend here, even though Nicolò had his mind on the championship. I realized, though, just how hard it is to win by such a wide margin: at a certain point, you start thinking about silly things..."

items.title: Bulega: “Hitting rock bottom shaped me as a person and as a rider”
items.author: Daniela Piazza
items.excerpt: “After the checkered flag, I started crying. I grew up in this paddock, and today I’m the World Champion. It’s an incredible story. This title is for those who believed in me during the tough times.”

items.title: Igna said: "Bulega isn't the same as he used to be; he's learned a lot."
items.author: Matteo Aglio
items.excerpt: On the future SBK regulations: “The best solution is not to limit who wins, but to give those who are struggling a chance to improve.”

items.title: Bulega, from hell to heaven: World Championship of one, none, and a hundred thousand
items.author: Daniela Piazza
items.excerpt: As Toprak’s designated successor, Nicolò lived up to expectations, bringing Italy back to the top of Superbike, 14 years after Biaggi. This marks the culmination of a journey that will lead him to reunite with Rossi and return to where it all began.

items.title: Petrucci: “I’m sad because I’m saying goodbye to Superbike in the worst possible way”
items.author: Daniela Piazza
items.excerpt: “I don’t know which way to go with this bike anymore. I knew that by coming here I could either win or quit, but a year ago I would have bet a hundred times on BMW: I’m where I’ve wanted to be for two years.”

items.title: Lecuona: "No one has Dall'Igna's mindset; this victory—and more—is proof of that"
items.author: Riccardo Guglielmetti
items.excerpt: "The secret is to always listen to everyone—a mindset that’s different from the Japanese. It took me a year to build up this confidence on the Ducati. I didn’t think I’d win by 5 seconds."

items.title: Surra: “I screwed up, but Acosta and Marquez also make mistakes”
items.author: Daniela Piazza
items.excerpt: “I’d never been up at the front like that before; I had everything under control, and maybe that’s why I made a mistake. It’s all part of the process. Pole position? I thought I could do it, but Lecuona and Bulega are better prepared than I am.”

items.title: Bulega: “I’m not completely comfortable on the Ducati: I’m riding at 90%”
items.author: Riccardo Guglielmetti
items.excerpt: “Sometimes you have to be smart and avoid doing stupid things. I didn’t think Iker had that much leeway. We’ll see tomorrow, though.”

items.title: Toprak: "This year reminds me of my first year in SBK, when I thought about quitting."
items.author: GPOne
items.excerpt: "For me, it's even tougher now than it was in 2018, because I've won three titles—I'm used to winning. Back then, finishing 12th was bad, but not as bad as it is now. The Michelins? I just can't get the softs to work."

items.title: Luzzi: “Márquez has Stoner’s talent and Lorenzo’s determination”
items.author: GPOne
items.excerpt: The engineer, who has worked with all three, describes the qualities that make them champions: Jorge’s determination, Casey’s raw talent and Marc’s ability to combine both.

items.title: THE BOOK Johann Zarco, victory and forgiveness
items.author: GPOne
items.excerpt: Written in collaboration with Michel Turco, it is the result of 10 hours of interviews. There could be a sequel.

items.title: Lecuona: “For the first time, I can say that I’m really enjoying riding the Ducati”
items.author: Daniela Piazza
items.excerpt: “I rode in my own style; I’m consistent and had a little margin to work with. Bulega’s stats? I looked at them—he always does something better than I do. I feel stronger than I did at Donington, so why not aim for the win?”

items.title: Surra: "The V4-S and the Superbike? The only thing they have in common is the Ducati name—everything else is different."
items.author: Riccardo Guglielmetti
items.excerpt: "The two bikes are totally different. I'm feeling confident about tomorrow, but I'm not saying anything. Today, my crew chief worked some magic on the bike."

items.title: Bulega: “The crashes? It’s strange what happened today on the Ducati”
items.author: Riccardo Guglielmetti
items.excerpt: “The Panigale was bouncing around, but maybe we've figured out why. The title celebration? I don’t want to know anything about it: they can even dress me up as Spider-Man or Superman.”

items.title: Dixon: “I’m not going through hell for nothing—this MotoGP burns young riders out”
items.author: Daniela Piazza
items.excerpt: “Riders start so early that by the time they’re 30, they’re already burned out. My wife’s illness has given me motivation and makes me believe that one day we’ll be champions. Redding? You have to build your own path.”

items.title: Zambenedetti: “The new regulation will be drastic and will eliminate Ducati’s advantage”
items.author: Riccardo Guglielmetti
items.excerpt: INTERVIEW - “The engine will be completely different, and we’ll face more challenges, but we’re working on it. If Superbike turns the tables, we have to ask ourselves if it’s still the right championship for Ducati.”

items.title: Pirro: “Bulega the favorite in the MotoGP? It’s just pre-race tactics. Testing isn’t the same as racing.”
items.author: Daniela Piazza
items.excerpt: “It’s too early to judge. We’ll see how things stand once we have some solid data. Ducati was expected to struggle at Misano but dominated. At Spielberg, it was expected to win easily but struggled. There’s no logic to it. We’re taking it one day at a time.”

items.title: Dall'Igna: "A lackluster performance by all the Ducatis in Austria"
items.author: GPOne
items.excerpt: "Marquez missed the podium due to a technical issue. Bagnaia's 7th-place finish is a sign of tenacity and pride. In this championship, you have to be willing to endure hardship."

items.title: Bulega: “Pol Espargarò? There’s not much to say really—it’s not true that the Ducati 850 is made for me.”
items.author: Riccardo Guglielmetti
items.excerpt: “There’s no rule that prevents a Superbike rider from testing a MotoGP bike. DAZN? If I want to say something that won’t be heard, I won’t say it in front of a camera.”

items.title: Lecuona: “Next year will be completely different on the Ducati”
items.author: Daniela Piazza
items.excerpt: “Michelin tyres perform differently than Pirellis, so the bike handles differently and needs to be ridden differently. I’ve tried every chance I’ve had to beat Bulega, and I’ll do the same here at Cremona.”

items.title: Bassani: “Bulega’s Lamborghini? I had to pay for my car”
items.author: Riccardo Guglielmetti
items.excerpt: “Nicolò deserves that car; if they don’t give it to him, who should they give it to? Ducati has done an incredible job this year. The 2027 Bimota is a little different.”

items.title: Petrucci: “Racing in the Superbike doesn’t make sense anymore if they ask you for money”
items.author: Riccardo Guglielmetti
items.excerpt: “The MotoAmerica BMW is nothing like the Ducati from four years ago. BMW asked me to race and be a test rider. I’ll make a decision this weekend.”

items.title: Quadranti: “MV Agusta? It’s like fighting windmills. The future of Arenas isn’t up to me.”
items.author: Riccardo Guglielmetti
items.excerpt: INTERVIEW – “I chased the title with MV Agusta for ten years. Returning to Superbike with Arenas? It’s something to consider: I know Albert wants to race in SBK, but his future isn’t in my hands.”

items.title: Filippo Bianchi racing in 2027 Sportbike World Championship with Prodina XCI Racing
items.author: GPOne
items.excerpt: The 21-year-old from Tuscany will joining as the Italian champion in his class, making his debut on a Kawasaki Ninja ZX-6R 636: “It’s the fulfillment of a dream I’ve had since I was a child.”

items.title: Torres: “I was in danger of not racing this year; this is the beginning of a great story”
